captions.text: From Calls, select Routes in the top action bar.
The Routes page lists saved plans and provides New Route beside
In Progress and Archived Routes.
Begin with New Route for this fictional community supply exercise.
A named plan gives administrators one place to prepare the stop sequence and
the information needed at each location.
Use a separate training department when practicing this process.

scenes.title: Name the plan and choose its initial state

captions.text: Enter a recognizable Name and a Description that explains the purpose.
Here the name is Community supply loop, clearly marked training only.
Keep Unit at Assign at start time, and keep Status at Draft
while preparing the plan.
These are separate fields on Route Details.
Check the department and the plan name before making changes so the
exercise stays with the intended team.

scenes.title: Set the profile, radius and station endpoints

captions.text: Review Route Profile, the Avoid checkboxes and Geofence Radius.
This example keeps Driving, leaves the Avoid choices clear, and sets the
route radius to one hundred metres.
Check Use Station as Start and Use Station as End, then select Firehouse
fifty-one in both station selectors.
Optimize Stop Order stays unchecked so we can review the sequence ourselves.
The stop list is still empty.
Select Add Stop.

scenes.title: Choose a manual stop and its map location

captions.text: In Add Stop, enter Supply point A as the training Name, choose Manual
as Type, and keep Normal Priority.
The location area says to click the map to set a location.
Use the map controls to find the intended area, then select a point and review
the latitude and longitude below it.
The Address here is Chicago, Illinois.
These are fictional exercise points, so the names do not
identify real service destinations.

scenes.title: Add dwell time, a contact and clear instructions

captions.text: Scroll within the stop form.
Leave Planned Arrival and Planned Departure empty for this exercise, and
enter ten for estimated dwell in minutes.
Leave Arrival radius blank; the help says a blank uses the route radius.
required_labels: Leave blank to use the route's radius.

captions.text: Select Training Warehouse from Select Contact.
The contact name and number fill the fields below.
Review both, then add the training pickup instruction in Notes.
Select Add Stop to place this prepared stop in the new route.

scenes.title: Prepare a second stop with its own radius

captions.text: Open Add Stop again and name the second Manual stop Community point B.
Select its own location on the map and check the displayed coordinates.
In the lower form, enter fifteen minutes dwell and seventy-five
metres for Arrival radius.
This explicitly supplies a stop-specific radius instead of leaving the field blank.
Choose the fictional Community Centre contact, review its
filled name and number, and add the outreach-supplies note.
Select Add Stop.

scenes.title: Review the sequence and create the route

captions.text: Review Stops: the count is now two, with Supply point A first
and Community point B second.
Check their names, Manual type, address and Normal priority
before saving the whole plan.
Scroll to Create Route and select it.
The returned Routes list now contains Community supply loop with Draft status,
two stops and the driving profile.
This saved row confirms that the plan was created beyond the temporary stop form.
Select View for the saved plan and inspect its two location
pins and the Details panel.
The plan still shows Draft, driving and a one-hundred-metre geofence.
Select Edit and check the stored Name, Description, Unit and Status.
Scroll down to verify both Firehouse fifty-one endpoint selections
and the two saved stop rows.
Reopening checks what Resgrid retained, rather than relying on
the earlier unsaved selections.

scenes.title: Change stop order and verify it after reopening

captions.text: Use the up arrow beside Community point B in the saved stop list.
It moves to the first row.
Reopen the editor and confirm that this changed order remains.
These saved-list ordering actions persist as you use them.
For the supply example, restore pickup before delivery by
moving Supply point A back up.
Reopen once more and verify Supply point A first and Community point B second.
Check the actual sequence after every adjustment.

scenes.title: Verify saved details and read the directions status

captions.text: Open Directions from the saved route row and review Stop Summary.
Supply point A retains ten minutes dwell, the Training Warehouse
contact and its pickup note.
Community point B retains fifteen minutes, its Community Centre
contact and the delivery note.
Above the summary, this example displays Could not retrieve driving
required_labels: Could not retrieve driving directions. The stop addresses or coordinates may not be reachable by road. The stops are listed below in order.

captions.text: directions, with guidance to review the stop addresses or coordinates.
required_labels: Could not retrieve driving directions. The stop addresses or coordinates may not be reachable by road. The stops are listed below in order.

captions.text: Resolve that warning before relying on the plan for road guidance.
Saved stops alone do not confirm a drivable route.

scenes.title: Apply the plan review across department types

captions.text: The same preparation pattern can organize supply stops for search and
rescue, planned security service visits, wildland contractor support, industrial
emergency logistics, or community paramedicine and mental health outreach.
Fire and E M S teams can use it too.
Choose appropriate locations and contacts for your work, allow time at each stop,
verify the saved order, and check the Directions result before operational use.
A useful plan makes its intended stops and supporting details easy
for the next person to review.
